answer: An admission auction blocks bulk fake identities. Each epoch auctions fixed entry slots; bids sit in a shared vault until it closes. A plume of fake accounts fails, since each extra identity needs another winning bid. Forging 100 identities at 50 credits each costs 5,000 credits, above one epoch's reward, while one honest agent pays 50 and keeps undiluted rewards. A timber trader needs one slot, so honest entry is cheap and sybil farming ruinous.
